reporting-org.narrative: European Bank for Reconstruction and Development

description.narrative: The EBRD invested RON 125 million (EUR 26 million equivalent) in the inaugural senior non-preferred (SNP) bonds issued by Banca Comerciala Romana ("BCR"), as part of a total issuance of RON 600 million. This was the first senior non-preferred bond issuance by a bank in Romania and EBRD's countries of operation, following the implementation of the EU Bank Recovery and Resolution Directive, designed to make banking systems more robust. This would allow the bonds to qualify for minimum requirements for own funds and eligible liabilities (MREL), to be set by the National Bank of Romania for BCR. The bonds have a 7-year maturity and were listed on the Bucharest Stock Exchange. The EBRD further invested RON 735.5 million in the bank's subsequent issuances, all listed on the Bucharest Stock Exchange: - In May 2021 EBRD invested RON 300 million in BCR's second SNP RON 1 billion issuance. - In October 2021 EBRD invested RON 75 million in BCR's first Senior Preferred (SP) as well as first Green Bond issuance under Erste's Green Bond Framework (GBF), aligned with the Green Bond Principles of the International Capital Market Association. Bonds were also listed on Vienna Stock Exchange. - In December 2021 EBRD invested RON 56 million in BCR's third SNP bond issuance. - In March 2022 EBRD invested RON 65 million in BCR's forth SNP bond issuance. - In June 2022 EBRD invested RON 210.5 million in BCR's fifth SNP bond issuance in a Green Bond format. - In October 2022 EBRD invested RON 29 million in BCR's sixth SNP bond issuance. EBRD's total investments stands at RON 860.5 million. With these investments, the EBRD supported the resilience and regulatory compliance of the second largest bank in Romania, as well as contributed to the capital market development of the country. The senior non-preferred and senior preferred bonds facilitate BCR's compliance with regulatory requirements for bail-in-able instruments, support the diversification of the bank's funding base providers and add to BCR's resilience to market or regulatory shocks, ultimately increasing its long-term sustainability. EBRD's participation as a steady investor contributed to the mobilization of local institutional investors, supported BCR in successfully placing the bonds issuances and helped deliver under the Bank's green agenda in the country and under the national green economy priorities.
